pull.title: kernel: document that blocks cache their check results
pull.body:
`CheckBlock` returns true right away when `block.fChecked` is set. In the kernel API a `btck_Block` wraps a shared `CBlock`, and `btck_block_copy` only adds a reference, so once a block passed `btck_block_check` or `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block`, later calls on it (or on a copy) skip the checks, whatever consensus params or flags are passed. For example a regtest block that has passed once with regtest params also returns 1 from `btck_block_check` with mainnet params.

bitcoind isn't affected, since it only has one chainstate manager and one set of params. `btck_block_check` and custom signet params are new in 32.0, and the header docs don't mention this.

Following sedited's review, this no longer copies the block on every call. It only documents on `btck_block_check` and `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` that a block caches its check results and should only be used with one set of consensus parameters.

The only overhead is that a block passed in a second time re-runs the context-free checks instead of returning early; for a duplicate `process_block` call, `AcceptBlock` still returns early on `fAlreadyHave`, so nothing is re-stored or re-connected.

Left some nits.

Thanks for the review! Took both suggestions in ac8a65d939: the signet test now also asserts BlockValidationResult::CONSENSUS, and the note is added to the docs of btck_block_check and btck_chainstate_manager_process_block in bitcoinkernel.h.

I tested ac8a65d939 with -DBUILD_KERNEL_LIB=ON. I ran the new tests with bitcoinkernel.cpp from the parent, ed7dd7cf4e, and test_kernel failed. When I put this commit's file back, it passed.

The description says 4 failures, and I saw 5. The extra check is the CONSENSUS result at test_kernel.cpp:1118, which wasn't in 9d735dae.

Should this be backported to 32.x? btck_block_check is new in that release.

ACK ac8a65d939

Thanks for testing! You're right, the fifth one is the `CONSENSUS` assertion I added after yuvicc's review; I updated the description.

On backporting: `btck_block_check`, `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` and `btck_chain_parameters_create_signet` are all in 32.x, so the issue is present in the 32.0 release and I think a backport makes sense. Happy to open one if maintainers want it.

Approach NACK

I don't think this is a worthwhile fix. The same problem exists in the normal unit tests as well, and shouldn't be fixed there with this approach either in my opinion. Paying a copy for every check call to protect against a scenario that should never happen, does not seem worthwhile to me.

kernel: document that blocks cache their check results

A btck_Block caches the result of its context-free checks, and copies
made with btck_block_copy share that cache. Once a block passed
btck_block_check or btck_chainstate_manager_process_block, later calls
with other consensus parameters or flags are not checked again.

Document that a block should only be used with a single set of
consensus parameters, instead of paying for a copy on every call.

events.body:
Thanks for the review, sedited. You're right: a copy on every call isn't worth it for a case that shouldn't happen, and the unit tests have the same property.

I dropped the copy and the tests. The PR is now a single docs commit (54b363a291, rebased on current master, which also clears the conflict). It states on `btck_block_check` and `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` that a `btck_Block` caches its check results, that copies from `btck_block_copy` share the cache, and that a block should only be used with one set of consensus parameters.

I changed the title and description to match. If you'd rather not have the note either, I'm happy to close this.
